text.en:
Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 10th June 2004 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

Milled and bearing the words “MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE” and lion symbol.
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the yeardate “2004” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’clock for the $10 gold and $10 silver coins.
The main feature of the coin is the “Harmony” sculpture at the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park (CS-SIP) that was jointly unveiled by SM Lee Kuan Yew and China’s Vice-Premier Li Lanqing in 2001 to symbolise the close bilateral relations. The “Harmony” sculpture resembling the figure “8”, symbolises “prosperity” and “abundance” for CS-SIP and its tenants.

The words “CHINASINGAPORE SUZHOU INDUSTRIAL PARK” in English and Chinese, above and below the sculpture respectively, signify the central theme of the coin.
The ’$10’ denomination to the left of the sculpture and the words “10th Anniversary” in English and Chinese to the right provide the overall balance to the design.
